newsitem.title: UK: Wassall rises on upbeat trading outlook.
newsitem.headline: Wassall rises on upbeat trading outlook.

text.p: Shares in Wassall Plc were up 13-1/2p at 306p by 0805 GMT, lifted by a positive trading statement as well as a hefty increase in first-half profits and dividend, dealers and analysts said.
"The company is bullish about its future prospects which is what the market is concentrating on," one dealer said.
Wassall chief executive Christopher Miller said in his results statement: "The outlook is very positive and gives us great confidence for the future."
The industrial cable group reported a 36 percent increase in profits before tax and exceptional items to 24.5 million stg and a 35 percent jump in the first-half dividend to 2.1 pence.
Analyst Zafar Khan at SG Strauss Turnbull agreed that the trading statement was bullish but was disappointed by the firm's failure to hedge against a fall in the price of copper.
"They lost eight million stg due to the fall in the copper price during the period and they say they will lose another 14 million stg or so in the second half," Khan said.
"Other companies hedge against this sort of thing. I think they really should explain why they don't do so," he added.
Wassall said that by 31 December 1995, an increase in the price of copper, which it uses to manufacture cable, had led to a cumulative stockholding gain of 22.1 million stg.
A subsequent drop in the price of copper this year however is expected to reverse that gain by the end of the second half of the year.
